note: ep09 Short 2 (2026-11-07): about one minute, one story only: Uncle Tu's wait-for-a-10%-drop rule vs Minh buying every paycheck, starting at the October 2007 record. Built so the founder can alternate two Shorts through the week (the 2:13 vertical is Short 1). Same ledger and conventions as the long; every spoken number checked by tools/validate-ep09-story.mjs. Replay lines carry `month` (months since 2007-10). Speakers: N narrator, M Minh, T Uncle Tu. The family are illustrations.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Stocks at a record. Wait for a dip? Uncle Tu keeps his *five hundred dollars* a month in cash until the market is ten percent down. Minh just buys every paycheck.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: October two thousand seven. A record, right before the worst crash since the Great Depression. Waiting should win, right?

lines.speaker: T
lines.text: January two thousand eight. Ten percent down. *I buy.*

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: March two thousand nine. I bought right into the crash. I'm down by about a third.

lines.speaker: T
lines.text: Twenty thirteen. A new record. I stop buying.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: For more than six years, his paychecks piled up in cash: *thirty-eight thousand dollars*.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: June twenty twenty-six. Minh's way wins, by about *twenty-five thousand dollars*. The crash didn't cost Uncle Tu. Waiting did.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Every thirty-year window since eighteen seventy-one: waiting for a dip won *less than one time in four*. Would you wait? Tell me in the comments.
